# /crav1-tasks-ready-to-build

lane: cross-cutting | group: Start | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.54.0 | prompts: 0
purpose: List the tasks ready to build, for one spec or all, and why the others are blocked. Rewrites each slice build map.
use_when: You want to know which tasks can be built now, and why the others cannot, or you want the build map
reads: Reads, for one slice or every slice under `docs/specs/`, the open questions in `spec.md` with their `Blocks:`, `Asked:`, `Pending:`, and `Answered:` lines, the `Reviewed:` line, `## Approach`, and `## Risks` in `plan.md`, the task lines in `tasks.md` with their ticks, `(after: T#)`, `(branch:)`, `(step:)`, and `(map:)`, a `task: T#` title in `work-item.md` when that file exists, `claims.md` when it exists (`In progress:` lines), and `verify.md` when it exists. It fetches the specs repo before it reads.
writes: Writes a list in the chat with summary counts, Ready and Held grouped by build-map branch, Waits in order, Blocked, Needs verify, a Done count, one Next line per ready branch, and its source, plus one line pointing at the build map. Every run rewrites `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md`. The Tasks field is `T#` plus the short name. The word `build-map` prints only the short summary of that file. `open-map` writes a temp page and `export-map` one HTML file outside the repo.
leaves alone: Leaves every file other than `build-map.md` alone, including `verify.md` and `claims.md`, except the `(map:)` or `(after:)` marks a confirmed `fix-loop` writes in `tasks.md`, and never reads Azure Boards. It fetches the specs repo first. It does not commit the map.
limits: does not guess a dependency or a blocking link from task text. Where nothing is recorded it uses a fallback and marks the reason inferred. It writes no readiness marks except a confirmed `fix-loop`; review-plan, tighten-plan, plan-from-spec, and resolve-open-questions write them. The map is written only by `scripts/build_map.py`.
flow:
- a held task quotes the question's own `Q` or `question` line, not a statement or a reply.
- A waits-on list is T numbers only, for example `waits on T3, T5`.
- Who is the `Ask` or `owner` line, and the runner only when none is recorded.
- Held lists every held task, including one whose only wait is an `(after:)` on a task that is not built yet.
- the readiness ending leaves out `/crav1-build-tasks builds one task without the walk.`; `/crav1-help status` names it.
- when the merge list holds a pull request you opened, Run next leads with it, for example `Merge your PRs 71 and 73 first:` above `/crav1-merge-pr 71`, above the entry that resumes the walk; with none of yours nothing is added.
- A PR's owner is who opened it (the PR note's `author:`, else `PR author:` in build-progress), not the claimer: `PR 71 (person A's, you added T5)`, or `owner not recorded`; others' PRs get `Waiting: PR 71 and PR 73 are person A's; they unblock T8.` A blank line separates the numbered list from the Waiting line under it.
- When none of the listed pull requests is yours, Run next leads with `Ask the PR owners to merge, in this order:` and one line per owner, such as `- person B: PR 82`, above the entry that resumes the walk.
- A PR with no recorded author is read from its own host (`gh` or `az`, read-only, short timeout) and recorded as `PR author:` in build-progress by `walk_progress.py pr-author`; when the host does not say, the skill asks once who opened it and records the answer the same way.
- With the repo known, one read-only host lookup (`gh` or `az`, 8-second timeout) gives both who opened a pull request and whether it merged, and the owner is recorded as `PR author:`; the skill asks who opened it only when that lookup names no one, offering the names the kit already knows (claims, PR notes, build-progress authors and owners) and `Don't know`.
- `build-map.md` colours each branch box by its worst task: green done (solid edge), amber waits on a pull request or a question (dashed edge), red truly blocked (thick edge), blue ready or not started, with a legend and bright edges and text for a dark background.
- on Windows the host lookup runs `az.cmd` by its full path, with no prompts and a 20-second timeout, so a completed pull request on Azure DevOps is read as merged.
- When a host cannot be read the ready check says why under Catch up first, with the fix command alone under its label (`az login`, `az extension add --name azure-devops`), lists the pull requests under `host_unread`, sets `ask_first` to `host`, and does not ask who opened them.
- An answer to `pr-author` or `code-repo` goes into that pull request's own build-progress file, picked by branch, and the reply names the file to commit.
- Owner choices add the people open questions wait on and never offer `other`, a team or an organisation.
- one shared module, `task_state.py`, owns a task's state (done, tick pending, waits for a merge, open) for the ready check, the build map (each task's state and each box colour), verify's tick and finalize-commit.
- A built task waiting on its pull request is waiting, never a silent blocker; an unrecognized blocker counts as Blocked and is printed.
- A task that waits on a task that ticks only when its own branch's pull request merges is a merge deadlock: Blocked, red on the map, with `/crav1-tighten-plan` in Run next.
- A pull request whose branch still has an open task waiting on another pull request says `not ready to merge: T46 waits on T8 (PR 73)` and is listed after it.
- Held lines name every unfinished dependency, then `and T8 (not built)`.
- The map is written before uncommitted files are counted, and the line reads `Commit the <n> changed spec files:`.
- Owner names drop a leading word like `Admin` and a trailing `(...)` tag, on write and on read, stored `PR author:` lines are rewritten once, and the reply ends with a `Recorded:` line naming the files written.
- A merged or completed pull request gets a merge-pr result in its build-progress file, so its tasks are done and it leaves the merge list in that run; a closed one reads `Waiting: PR <n> was closed without merging; its tasks are not done.`; one with no recorded code repo reads `code repo not recorded`, and the skill asks once which repo, records it with `walk_progress.py code-repo --root <spec-folder> --pr <n> --repo <name-or-url>` and runs the check again.
- `Build map:` ends `(updated)` or `(unchanged, nothing new since the last write)`.
- open pull requests are one `Merge these PRs, in this order:` block, one numbered PR per line with its owner (`yours` or the name) and what merging it ticks and lets start, in dependency order.
- Branch runs reads `built, PR <n> open`.
- A task verified on an unmerged branch reads `verified on <branch>, waits for PR <n> to merge`.
- branch entries read `Build <T# full name> on <branch>:` above the command; a held task quotes its whole question; a question that says `Raised with` or `Waiting for` a person counts as asked; uncommitted slice files add `Commit the walk's changes, <n> files:` above `/crav1-finalize-commit` before the push; task titles keep their code text with no stray ` ,` or ` )`.
- a claimed task that is built on a branch that is not merged reads `built by <name>, waits for PR <n> to merge` in the Held list and on `build-map.md`, not `in progress by <name> since <date>`.
- A reopened step's entry gives the reason in one plain sentence above `Finish the reopened <command> step:`.
- a done task's commit is its branch's `merge-pr` result in `build-progress`, never a later tick or commit step's hash; that hash is only a last fallback and never replaces a mark.
- A branch whose open tasks are all claimed or walked reads `built, waits for PR <n> to merge` or `in progress` on `build-map.md`, never `held, waits on` its own tasks.
- `Delivers:` and `Tasks:` lines use full names.
- a done task's mark on the build map takes its commit only from its own evidence: the merge result in its branch's `build-progress` file, else its own row in `verify.md`.
- A Date line, a gaps note or another task's row never lends its commit.
- Held and ready lines show full task names, never cut with `...`.
- readiness reads `build-progress/<branch>.md`: a task whose branch's last step is `comment` or `wait-merge` waits for its pull request to merge and is not in `can_start`.
- Your own claim reads `T5 is yours; the walk resumes it.` or `T5 is yours and waits for PR 71's merge.` Ready branches carry full task names.
- A branch description is never a planning note such as `cut from develop after ...`, and never a sentence about a done task.
- the Catch up first line `T# failed verify: <reason>.` is short.
- The reason is the Verify cell's opening sentence, plus the sentence that names the cause (`...
- made the asserts stale.`, `...
- because ...`) when it fits, about 200 characters, cut only at a sentence end; leading run detail (`fail at PR 7's tip abc1234: pipeline 6 run 251, 110 failed, 173 passed.`) gives way to the next sentence.
- The full cell stays in `verify.md`.
- A held question or approval with nobody named says `Nobody is named to answer it yet.` or `Nobody is named to give it yet.`, and the Waiting line says `nobody named for 1`, never `Waiting for not named yet`.
- a fresh verify is never behind.
- An older `Next:` line in `verify.md` is stale only for a ticked task whose own row says Not implemented, claimed done or unverified, or has no row; a Verified or Failed row is current.
- A built task whose verify failed is `T# failed verify: <reason>.` in the Catch up first block, with `Fix T#:` and `/crav1-fix-build-gaps <slug> T#`.
- Needs verify holds only its own task, so ready branches keep their blocks (the result is ready-partial), and questions not asked yet stay a `/crav1-show-or-ask-open-questions <slug>` entry after them.
- The Catch up first block never replaces the branch blocks.
- what you can fix now with one command leads Run next as a `**Catch up first**` block, before the branch blocks and in their layout: verify.md behind tasks.md, a verify.md row for a T# not in tasks.md, and a specs repo ahead of origin.
- One or two plain sentences, then each command alone under its label: `/crav1-verify-build-against-spec <slug>` (it checks the behind tasks and drops the stray row, so they share one command) and `git push`, then a `---` line before the first branch block.
- Up to three clean sentences from the plan step, about 300 characters, cut only at a sentence end; else the plan note's opening clause (before the first `:` or ` — `, a person lead such as `Person A builds PR 73:` dropped); else the step's heading; else one sentence from the open task names, about 160 characters.
- Left out only with no plan step and no usable task name; a person's name never shows.
- A held question that ends with `:` or only points to a note shows the quoted question under it (the `>` blockquote, else quoted text after the colon, else the first sentence ending in `?`).
- A `---` line stands between two branch blocks.
- Open tasks are listed in the order the walk runs them; a task that cannot start yet says why, `(waits on T5)`, and the task command then names `the first task that can start`.
- Long sentences and held questions are cut at a clause end or a word, about 160 characters, never on a dangling word, and a held question that opens with a heading such as `Client certificate.` shows the question itself.
- the loop-fix card and Waiting lines follow the card wording rule in `docs/reference/question-cards.md`.
- Held tasks in the ending are one per line under their branch, with the open question shortened to its first sentence, about 100 characters at most.
- Run next is one block per ready branch: the bold branch, one plain sentence from its plan step, its open tasks, then `Run the whole branch:` and `Run only T#, the first task:` (or `Run T#:`), each command alone under its label.
- Under `Build map:` the reply offers `Zoom the map in your browser:` with `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build <slug> open-map`.
- `scripts/kit-lint.py` checks this skill's cards.
- On this skill: `fix-loop`, `fix-loop <n>`, `open-map`, `export-map` and `pipeline-runs`.
- The script flags `--fix-loop` and `--export` are unchanged.
- The same hyphen-only rule applies to the kit's other choice words, including `release-claim`, `new-branch`, `one-task`, `git-log` (the style word), and the rest listed in the 1.163.0 changelog.
- A successful `walk_progress.py fix-loop` preview (no `--yes`) exits 0.
- The loop-fix `Why:` line is a plain reason with no keyword list.
- A not-ready ending starts with `Run next:` for the first real next step, in plain words.
- `open-map` shows the whole `build-map.md` as a zoomable page in the browser, the text in a readable column and each Mermaid diagram in place, full window width, with wheel zoom, drag to pan, Fit, 100% and Fullscreen.
- `export-map` writes one self-contained HTML file to share, `<slug>-build-map-<YYYY-MM-DD>.html` in Downloads, never inside the specs repo.
- The script is `scripts/open_build_map.py docs/specs/<slug>` (`--export`, `--out`, `--no-open`).
- It loads Mermaid 11.4.1 and marked 18.2.0 from `scripts/vendor/`, or from jsDelivr when that folder is missing; the export inlines both.
- A done branch says `Waited for:` instead of `Waits for:`.
- (Until 1.183.0 the map file also had one line under its heading naming both commands.)
- `build_map.py --recommend` reads remotes with `git ls-remote --heads` once per run, besides the `origin/<name>` refs, and, when `gh` works, the open pull requests.
- A task-line branch deleted only locally is offered, not replaced by a new step-named branch: `because: <name> is on origin only; checkout creates the local tracking branch`, then a last `checkout: <name>` line.
- An open pull request whose head is the name wins over merged and deleted, and a `PR n` on the task line picks it.
- A remote that cannot be read is never taken as gone.
- `CRAV1_NO_REMOTE_CHECK=1` turns the remote reads off.
- The branch is checked in the task's code repo, which can be a separate checkout from the specs repo: a repo prefix on `(map:)`/`(branch:)`, a Match `Branch: <repo> <branch>` line, or a `Repo:` line in tasks.md names it, and `--code-repo <path>`, the specs repo, or a sibling checkout with that name holds it.
- `repo: <path>` is printed when that is not the specs repo.
- When the named repo is not found, the line is `because: could not check <repo> from here`, never deleted.
- SKILL.md names each with a load-when line.
- **`/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`** reads `spec.md` open questions, `plan.md` (the `Reviewed:` line and `## Risks`), `tasks.md`, and `verify.md` for one slice or every slice.
- A ticked task is Done when `verify.md` lists it as verified, otherwise Needs verify.
- Then a task is blocked by a missing `plan.md`, by a kept-open question whose `Blocks:` line names it, by a kept-open question with no `Blocks:` line (tasks named in the text, or the whole slice only when none are named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded), by a plan Risk that says do not implement until resolved only when that question has no `Blocks:` line, or by an unticked task in its `(after: T#)` (recorded) or, with no `(after: …)`, the task just before it (inferred).
- `Blocks: none` blocks no task.
- Any `Blocks:` line wins over that Risk wording.
- Lists and Next follow dependency order: the `(after: …)` graph in waves, lowest number first in a wave; Next is the ready task that unblocks the most; a cycle blocks its tasks.
- It may run `scripts/task_order.py` and `scripts/question_blocks.py` next to the skill.
- Otherwise it is Ready, with a warning when the plan review is unknown (inferred) or still has open `P#`s.
- Shows summary counts per slice, then Ready and Held grouped by build-map branch, Waits in order, and Blocked (one reason each, recorded or inferred), Needs verify, a Done count, one `Next:` line per ready branch, and a `Source:` line.
- A cycle, or an after: that names no task, is Blocked.
- Local only: it never reads Azure Boards and names `/crav1-ado-sync` for task states there.
- an unapproved `## Approval needed` item holds its `Holds:` tasks.
- Other tasks still start (`ready-partial`).
- A matching `Approved:` line clears the hold.
- `task_order.py` lists them under Waiting on approval.
- shows a task's `(branch: …)` and one Branches line from local git only.
- the `Sub-branches:` and `left behind:` lines and `merged, reverted on <base> (<sha>)`, report only.
- the `Promotion:` line under the Branches line, with the optional `pipeline-runs` check.
- command-only (`disable-model-invocation: true`).
- It runs only when you type `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build`; the agent does not start it from a plain question, and its description no longer loads in every chat.
- `Blocks: none` blocks no task.
- A `Blocks:` line wins over a Risk that says do not implement until resolved.
- a Risk that says do not implement until resolved matches a question on the question first sentence, a `(question: <first words>)` tag, or the same Blocks tasks named in the Risk.
- `scripts/task_order.py --json` uses T1 style ids.
- `task_order.py` text uses the same Waits in order and Blocked headings.
- The interpreter is `docs/reference/running-scripts.md`.
- every run rewrites `docs/specs/<slug>/build-map.md` through `scripts/build_map.py`.
- The word `build-map` shows only the short summary: the path, how many branches in each wave can run in parallel, then the Overlap lines for that wave, one per pair.
- One branch per numbered Approach step, unless a task has `(map:)`.
- `(step:)` links a task to a step.
- A question hold is counted in the wave heading (`3 branches, 2 can start now`).
- An overlap note names two branches in one wave that share a `(spec:)` requirement or a backtick path.
- Who uses the 1.127.0 rule.
- A cycle or an unknown `(after:)` is under Blocked.
- the row branch is `(map:)`, else `(branch:)`, else the plan step, else `committed later on`, else `feat/<slug>-<words>`.
- `--recommend T#` prints that name and does not write.
- Tasks are short names (a `task: T#` title in `work-item.md`, else the text up to ` (`, `, in `, or the sentence end, about 80 characters).
- The wave heading is always `N branches, M can start now`, including `1 branch, 1 can start now`.
- A row whose task text names another branch adds `Task text names feat/x; built on feat/y`.
- That is `(map:)`, else `(branch:)`, else a `feat/…` name in the sentence, else `committed later on`.
- `from <base>` after the branch is its base.
- When the row is that task-line branch, the note is `Plan step names feat/orders-one-commit-cleanup-main; built on feat/orders-host-setup-scripts`.
- A `(map:)` row that is not the branch in the task text still says `Task text names feat/x; built on feat/y`.
- `--recommend` does not write.
- Later lines are `source: task line`, `source: build map`, or `source: new`, `from:` when the task line states a base, and `because:` when a merged or deleted branch was skipped.
- `--recommend` does not print that branch, including for that task.
- the result is `ready`, `ready-partial`, or `not-ready`.
- `ready-partial` lists the tasks that can start and where the hold begins.
- A task that waits on a held task is held too, reason `held, waits on T3`.
- `not-ready` is when nothing can start.
- The branch is `scripts/build_map.py --recommend T#`, so it matches the map.
- One `Next:` line per ready branch.
- A held line names the open question and who has it, or `held, waits on T3`.
- The Tasks field is `T#` plus the short name, and a done task is `~~T# short name~~ ✓ done` with its pull request.
- The walk record stays `Result: ready-partial`.
- `next_lines` recommend `/crav1-build-walk`, with the T number beside the short name and the branch, and name `/crav1-build-tasks` for one task without the walk.
- the ready check compares `tasks.md` with `verify.md`.
- A ticked task, or a task whose pull request is recorded merged (`(PR n)` and the word merged on the task line or its Match `Branch:` line), that `verify.md` still lists as not implemented, is behind.
- So is a `Next:` line in `verify.md` that names such a task.
- The check prints `Waiting: /crav1-verify-build-against-spec <slug> - verify.md is behind tasks.md (T2, T45)` and does not print that Next line.
- It does not write `verify.md`.
- `build-map.md` stays the one file this command writes.
- a `Next:` line is stale only when it names a ticked task.
- A ticked task still listed as `Not implemented` is behind, and so is a merged task still listed as `Not implemented`.
- A merged `[ ]` row whose status is `Implemented, verified, tick pending` is not behind.
- A verify-only change does not force `not-ready`.
- This command does not restamp `walk-progress.md`.
- Only the walk's record or `clear --yes` does.
- `scripts/task_order.py` lists a recorded-merged task under Needs tick.
- `scripts/resolve_spec.py` resolves a named spec: exact folder first, then one unique playbook basename, spec title, or work-item name.
- a question with no `Blocks:` line holds `T#` ids named in its text that exist in `tasks.md`, shown like a Blocks hold and noted inferred from the text.
- It holds the whole slice only when no task is named and resolve-open-questions has never been recorded.
- `Blocks: whole slice` (also `the whole slice`, any case) is a recorded hold of every unfinished task and stays Waiting through spec drift.
- A question with a `Blocks:` line, or one already recorded as waiting, stays Waiting through spec drift.
- `scripts/resolve_spec.py` also accepts one unique ordered token subsequence (`cc 1.0` matches `cc-process-1-0`).
- a named spec is `<interpreter> -X utf8 scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`.
- On Windows `<interpreter>` is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`.
- Elsewhere it is `python3`.
- `--recommend` is `scripts/build_map.py docs/specs/<slug> --recommend T#`.
- The rule is `docs/reference/running-scripts.md`.
- Behind or diverged, it stops and Run next is `git pull --no-rebase`.
- A task with an `In progress:` line in `claims.md` is held `in progress by <user> since <date>` and is not offered in Run next.
- A claim older than three days, or `Claim max age:`, warns and is never cleared on its own.
- A future line such as `(PR 12) to be merged into develop` is not a recorded merge.
- Next lines match Run next: the command alone in a code span, with the slug when `docs/specs` has several slices, and the branch and task on the next line.
- Task labels are never blank, and short names cut at a word boundary with an ellipsis.
- `task_order.py` prints short labels unless `--full` is passed.
- `M can start now` counts only ready branches.
- `approval_needed.py`, `question_blocks.py`, and `task_order.py` accept a spec folder or a file.
- `question_blocks.py` exits 0 when questions are found.
- Skills that document `scripts/repo_sync.py` or `scripts/claims.py` ship a wrapper to the build-walk copy.
- An open task is never placed under a branch git proves merged when another name is written for it.
- The ending has one Run next block at the top; the walk command appears only there; the reply prints that block verbatim and never writes a Next: line.
- `readiness --brief` prints only the result, a counts row, the ending, and claim warnings.
- A verify.md table row for a T# that is not in tasks.md is one Waiting line; the check does not edit verify.md.
- The map and the ready-check ending print one `Loop:` line per loop, naming the branches and the task line behind each direction of the wait, (since 1.161.0 followed by a fix offer, not a request to edit `tasks.md` by hand) The open tasks on those branches are Blocked in both, from one shared judgement, and are not offered in Run next.
- A branch always sits in a later wave than each branch it waits for, unless both are in the same loop.
- A held line shows the wave, or `in a loop`, never `(blocked)`.
- Run next offers each ready branch's next task, `/crav1-build-walk <slug> T#`, and, when that branch has two or more open tasks, the whole branch, `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <branch>`, as its own entry with `branch <branch>, every open task: …` underneath.
- `next_lines` carry the same entries.
- A `Branch runs:` block prints each unmerged `- Branch run:` status line from `walk-progress.md`.
- the readiness script prints the finished reply (`walk_progress.py readiness --root <spec-folder> --write-map --text`): the header, the counts row, `Result:`, the shared walk ending (Run next first, Held, Branch runs, Loop and Waiting lines, claim warnings), `Source:` and `Build map:`.
- The skill shows it as-is and never adds a `Next:` line.
- The brief reply is the default; the word `full` adds the per-task lists and the Order line.
- The rules moved to `references/rules.md`.
- The ending is shared with tighten-and-plan and build-walk through `scripts/walk_ending.py`.
- a loop no longer ends with a line telling you to edit `tasks.md` by hand.
- Under the `Loop:` line the reply offers fixes, best first, each in plain words: what is wrong, the change (build these tasks on the other branch, or let one task start without one wait), that the tasks stay the same and only the branch and pull request they go into change, and the order afterwards.
- Say `fix-loop` (the recommended fix) or `fix-loop <n>`.
- The card confirms, and on yes `walk_progress.py fix-loop --root <spec-folder> --pick <n> --yes` writes or replaces the `(map:)` marks, or removes the one `(after:)` wait, rebuilds `build-map.md`, and reports the loop gone or the next one.
- `tasks.md` and `build-map.md` stay uncommitted.
- `spec.md` is never touched.
- A ready or ready-partial reply also has a Run next entry, `/crav1-tasks-ready-to-build <slug> fix-loop`.
- `task_state.py` counts any done `Step: build T#` in a build-progress file as built and waiting for the merge, whatever the header lists, so older files work.
- A task already built on an unmerged branch is never startable and never reads `T# is yours; the walk resumes it.`; tasks that wait on it read `held, waits on PR <n> to merge (T#, recorded)`, and the merge list says the PR ticks every task on its branch.
- `Implemented, verified on branch` and `Implemented, verified, tick pending` are one state; both are read.
- `build-map.md` no longer has the two sentences above the diagram that named `open-map` and `export-map`; it starts with the heading and the grouping line, such as `One branch per plan step.` Both choice words still work.
- `task_state.py` treats a done plain `build` step whose result starts `done (T<n>:` as task T<n> built and waiting for the merge, so the ready check does not offer it, the merge list ticks every task on the branch, and tasks that wait on it wait on the pull request's merge.
- each branch block in `build-map.md` nests its lists: `- Tasks:` and `- Waits for:` are label bullets with one sub-bullet per item instead of items joined with `; `, a done task keeps its strike-through and `✓ done (PR N)` on its own sub-bullet, and an empty list is `Waits for: none` on one line.
- `task_state.walk_start` says whether the walk can start a task now.
- The ready check offers `/crav1-build-walk <slug> <T#>` only when it can (invariant I8), so the ready check and the walk agree.
- the open-task list, Run next and `build-map.md` name a task by its text up to the first verify item, through the shared `task_order.task_name`; unbalanced parentheses are dropped and stray spaces such as `( x` and `develop ,` are tidied.
- a free-text `(PR 12)` or `(PR 7 merged into develop)` does not mark a task done.
- Only a tick or the kit mark `(PR n, merged)` or `(PR n) merged` does.
- A task with `(after: T#)` stays held while that task's pull request is open, on the ready check and on the build map, and the held line says `waits for PR <n> to merge`.
- A task that says `(after: PR 87)`, or whose text says `after PR 87 merges`, stays held until the host says PR 87 is merged.
- The ready check, the build map and the walk ending all say `waits for PR 87 to merge`.
- When the code repo is not recorded, the check uses the same one-time repo question as 1.177.2.
- A pull request the host says is merged is cleared with `/crav1-build-walk <slug> T#`.
- A `--text` read that does not pass `--write-map` does not add a `PR author` line.

## Choice words
- question: Show the build map?
  - `build-map`: show only the build map for the same scope, such as cc 1.0; the task list stays off
- question: Show the full list?
  - `full`: the long form: every per-task list and the Order line; the brief reply is the default
- question: Fix the loop?
  - `fix-loop`: apply the recommended fix for branches that wait for each other, after the card confirms it
  - `fix-loop <n>`: apply the fix with that number from the Loop lines instead
- question: Open the map as a zoomable page?
  - `open-map`: open the whole build map in the browser, with a diagram you can zoom and pan
  - `export-map`: write the map as one HTML file to send, outside the specs repo
- question: Also check the latest pipeline runs?
  - `pipeline-runs`: check the latest successful Azure DevOps runs behind the Promotion line (read-only)
called_by: Called by the user with its slash command, any time (command-only).
runs by itself: Calls no skill.
